rule: good. context only and never parsed; texts 1 and 2 carry the rule and text 3 supplies the threads' origin, so the rule survives once the two edits below are made.
texts: mixed: the rule fires and every participant is covered, but the threads land in the slot for things an action creates or alters rather than the slot for things it deposits, so a later question about what the moth left on the lantern, asked as a transfer, finds nothing; the derived leaving is also keyed to the moth and the lantern rather than to the occasion, so two landings share one leaving. A plain deposit verb plus the per-occasion wording fixes both: 'Every time a nightmoth lands on a lantern, the nightmoth drops silken threads on the lantern.'

bad: 'rests on a lantern' is a bare position clause, which the instruction set treats as no happening at all, so the rule has no occasion to hang the shedding on — and the parse had to improvise, filing 'on the lantern' as an aboutness phrase instead of a place and recording the threads as something the moth created rather than deposited. Put the resting in the progressive (an explicit trigger that turns a position clause into a real state) and use a plain deposit verb: 'Whenever a nightmoth is resting on a lantern, the nightmoth drops silken threads onto the lantern.'
good. the explicit universal becomes a fireable per-thread rule, with the moth's underside as the source and the threads' silken-ness kept.
